title: Creating Magical Items
audit_comment: CHAPTER 4 of the DMO (printed pp. 86-95), the item-creation economy closing in one round: the holy water ceremony (the five-spell chain, the eight-hour meditations and rest, the -4 combat window, the one-font-one-week rule with the cost ladder and the Delsenora recycle read), the requirements doctrine (the class level thresholds, the common-rare-exotic materials and processes, the laboratory and altar economics), the Table 23 creation grid (28 rows of material, process, footnote, cost and time codes), the per-type details (the 70/80/60 bases, the potion and ring research windows, the ink ladder, the drained-item death rule), the recharge window with its -1 save-or-dust risk, the 96-00 automatic failure with the cursed-item twists, the Table 24 XP grid, and the Rozmare worked examples at 94 and 65 percent.

banner.title: CREATING MAGICAL ITEMS - DMO Chapter 4 closes: the holy water ceremony (the five-spell chain with the two reversed unholy forms, the eight-hour meditations, the chant turn, the -4 combat window, the one-font-one-week rule, the nine-row cost ladder with the Delsenora recycle read at 30 percent of 21,000 gp), the requirements doctrine (the wizard 9-and-11 and priest 7-9-11 thresholds, the specialist +5, the 5,000-gp laboratory with its 500-a-month upkeep, the 2,000-gp altar with its one-week vigil), the Table 23 grid (28 item rows of material, process, footnote, cost and time codes), the per-type success formulas (the 70/80/60 bases, the 1d3+1-week potion research at 100 gp a week, the 1d6+1-week ring research at 200 gp a week, the ink ladder, the scroll and ring reads, the drained-item death rule), the 24-hour recharge window with the -1 save-or-dust preparation risk, the 96-00 automatic failure with the cursed and creator curses, the Table 24 XP grid with its per-plus and special forms, and the Rozmare worked examples (the potion of speed at 94 percent, the long sword +1 +3 vs. regenerating creatures at 65 percent with its eight-week preparation).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 86-95 of the uploaded DMO session capture (part 1 holds printed 1-90, printed page N at OCR page N+1; part 2 holds printed 91-192, the 86-90 overlap resolved to the part 1 text); the holy water ceremony from pp. 86-87, the font cost ladder from p. 87, the level thresholds and working space from pp. 87-88, Table 23 from p. 89, the item details from pp. 90-92, the recharge and failure doctrine from pp. 92-93, Table 24 and the cursed values from pp. 93-94, the Rozmare examples from pp. 94-95. The potion success rule prints +1 percent for every two levels while the book's own Rozmare example works her 13th level at +26 percent, two percent a level; the printed rule and the worked read are both pinned with the divergence noted.
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 52 closed, 44 open - Chapter 4 is DONE in one round, ten boxes flip (nine children and the parent); the DMO arc continues with Chapter 5 (Magical Duels, pp. 96-117).

consts.comment: the Table 24 grid length: 27 item rows, potion single-use through weapon limited-use (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derUnholyReversedSpells
bools.comment: the reversed-spell rule: the spells marked with an asterisk are used in reversed form to create unholy water (printed p. 86).

bools.name: derCeremonyRuinOnDelay
bools.comment: the no-delay rule: any delay between finishing one spell and starting the next ruins the ceremony (printed p. 86).

bools.name: derCreateWaterOverflowDissipated
bools.comment: the overflow rule: the create water spell produces more water than the basin holds and the extra is channeled away or magically dissipated (printed p. 86).

bools.name: derFontDefileByCurse
bools.comment: the magical defilement: touching the font and casting a curse spell defiles it for holy water and magic font spells (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derFontDefileNonmagical
bools.comment: the mundane defilement: placing anything repugnant to the deity within the font defiles it nonmagically (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derDefiledFontRemade
bools.comment: the remade-font rule: a defiled font must be entirely remade; it cannot be cleansed or restored except by a wish (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derWarriorsRoguesCannot
bools.comment: the class bar: warriors and rogues cannot create magical items even with spellcasting ability (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derNoMagicalBooks
bools.comment: the writings bar: no character can make a magical book, libram, manual, tome or artifact (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derNoAbilityWritings
bools.comment: the writings bar: magical writings that increase levels and ability scores are likewise unbalancing (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derRacialItemsRacePriestOnly
bools.comment: the racial rule: racial items such as boots of elvenkind only by priests of the indicated race (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derPriestsCastStoredSpellsOk
bools.comment: the spell-source rule: priests and wizards can use spells on scrolls, stored in items or cast by other characters (printed p. 87).

bools.name: derOnlyUsableItems
bools.comment: the usability bar: priests and specialist wizards can make only items they can use - no cleric long swords, no transmuter wands of fire (printed p. 88).

bools.name: derVigilRestartOnInterrupt
bools.comment: the vigil restart: if interrupted, the vigil must be started over again (printed p. 88).

bools.name: derOnlyConsecratorUsesAltar
bools.comment: the altar monopoly: only the priest who performed the consecration can use it, no other creature while the priest lives (printed p. 88).

bools.name: derDefiledAltarReconsecrated
bools.comment: the defiled altar: if defiled, the priest must consecrate it again (printed p. 88).

bools.name: derDmApprovalRequired
bools.comment: the approval gate: the DM must approve any new magical item entering the campaign (printed p. 89).

bools.name: derItemFinestQuality
bools.comment: the quality rule: every item must be of the finest quality, specifically created to hold enchantment - no smithy sword becomes a frost brand (printed p. 90).

bools.name: derRequirementsNotAutoKnown
bools.comment: the hidden-requirements rule: the character does not automatically know what materials and processes are necessary (printed p. 90).

bools.name: derEnchantAndPermanencyRequired
bools.comment: the wizard chain: enchant an item to focus the energy, the power-duplicating spells, and most items also require permanency (printed p. 90).

bools.name: derPriestsPetitionDeities
bools.comment: the priest path: priests lack enchant an item and must petition their deities, the DMG Chapter 10 procedure (printed p. 90).

bools.name: derPriestNoConLossDefault
bools.comment: the priest read: priests do not normally suffer the loss, though the DM can rule the taxing process drains a point on permanency-class items (printed p. 90).

bools.name: derPotionDoseNotConsumed
bools.comment: the analysis dose: a full dose is needed but not consumed in the research (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derPotionFormulaReusable
bools.comment: the recorded formula: once personally researched and recorded, no re-research unless the record is lost (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derScrollNoSpellsCast
bools.comment: the scroll doctrine: no spells are actually cast in writing, but the writer must know the spell and hold the components (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derScrollComponentsConsumed
bools.comment: the scroll components: if normally consumed in casting, they are consumed in writing (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derScrollPenaltyCarried
bools.comment: the scroll penalty carry: a casting penalty such as magical aging carries into the scroll writing (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derScrollFailurePreservesSpells
bools.comment: the scroll failure: a failed spell fills the remaining space with an ink blob, leaving written spells intact (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derScrollNewQuillPerSpell
bools.comment: the scroll quill: a new quill must be used for each spell written (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derRingCommonProcessExtra
bools.comment: the ring read: any ring requires one common process beyond its Table 23 needs (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derRingPriestsSufferPenalty
bools.comment: the ring read: priests still suffer the spell penalty though they cast nothing - the complex enchantment is harder to petition (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derRodStaffWandPermanency
bools.comment: the rods-staves-wands chain: enchant an item, the power spells, and a permanency spell is required (printed p. 92).

bools.name: derDrainedItemDeadForever
bools.comment: the drained-item death: losing all charges kills the magic forever, even a rechargeable item can never be enchanted again (printed p. 92).

bools.name: derEachPlusSeparateSpell
bools.comment: the plus rule: each plus for a weapon or protective device requires a separate spell (printed p. 92).

bools.name: derSingleUseNoPermanency
bools.comment: the permanency exemption: single-use and limited-use items do not require permanency (printed p. 92).

bools.name: derMiscSameAsRing
bools.comment: the misc-armor-weapon base: the chance to create one of these is the same as for a ring (printed p. 92).

bools.name: derTimeNotReducible
bools.comment: the time doctrine: manufacturing time cannot be reduced by extra workers, help or money (printed p. 91).

bools.name: derMagesRechargeNoncasterItems
bools.comment: the recharge permission: mages can also recharge items usable only by fighters or rogues (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derRechargeSpellDuplicatesPower
bools.comment: the recharge doctrine: the spell must duplicate the item's power - the most powerful function for multi-function items, a cone of cold for a wand of frost (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derRechargeNormalCastingTime
bools.comment: the recharge timing: each spell takes its normal casting time, not the enchant an item delay (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derDmRollsSecretly
bools.comment: the secret roll: the DM secretly rolls the dice for each creation attempt (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derSuccessNeverImproves
bools.comment: the mastery limit: no matter how many times a character has created an item, the chances stay the same (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derFailureUsuallyRuins
bools.comment: the ordinary failure: most failed attempts ruin the item into useless slag (printed p. 93).

bools.name: derAutoFailMakesCurse
bools.comment: the 96-00 twist: the item appears normal but carries a cursed or reversed effect, DM's choice (printed pp. 93-94).

bools.name: derCursedCompareToSimilar
bools.comment: the cursed-item doctrine: judge cost and difficulty against useful items of similar power - a sword -2 is as hard as a sword +2 (printed p. 94).

bools.name: derCursedFailureDestroys
bools.comment: the cursed failure: a failed cursed-item attempt is destroyed (printed p. 94).

bools.name: derCreatorCursedOnAutoFail
bools.comment: the creator curse: a cursed-item attempt failing on 96-00 puts the curse on the creator, never a useful item (printed p. 94).

bools.name: derNonstandardCompareToSimilar
bools.comment: the nonstandard doctrine: assign an XP value by comparison to similar existing items; err high (printed p. 94).

tables.comment: the Table 23 creation grid (printed p. 89): 28 item rows, potion single-use through weapon limited-use; the material and process rarity codes, the footnote process, the cost in half-XP units and the time kind with its rate.
col_comments: the material code: 1 common, 2 rare, 3 exotic, 4 rare-and-common, 5 exotic-per-function, 6 exotic-per-use (printed p. 89).
the process code: 0 variable, 1 common, 2 rare, 3 exotic, 4 rare-and-common, 5 exotic-per-function, 6 exotic-per-use, 7 rare-per-function (printed p. 89).
the footnote process: 0 none, 1 the footnote-one common, 3 the footnote-two exotic, 4 the footnote-three rare-and-common (printed p. 89).
the cost in half-XP units: 1 half value, 2 the value, 4 double, 6 triple, 8 quadruple (printed p. 89).
the time kind: 1 day per 100 gp, 2 day per spell level, 3 fixed days, 4 week per 100 gp, 5 week per 1,000 gp (printed p. 89).
the time rate: the days or weeks of the time kind, or the fixed day count (printed p. 89).

tables.name: derT24Grid
tables.comment: the Table 24 typical experience values (printed p. 93): 27 item rows with the min and max XP and the special-form code - per plus, the value sum, the lower-plus-20-40-percent share and the per-spell-level read.
col_comments: the XP minimum: the low end of the range, or the per-plus and per-spell-level base (printed p. 93).
the XP maximum: the high end of the range, zero where a special form applies (printed p. 93).
the special-form code: 0 flat, 1 per plus, 2 lower value plus higher value, 3 lower value plus 20-40 percent of the higher, 4 per spell level (printed p. 93).

tables.name: derFontGrid
tables.comment: the holy water font cost ladder (printed p. 87): nine capacities, six through fifty vials; the basin cost as dice x multiplier plus bonus, the pedestal a flat fee.
col_comments: the basin cost dice count: one die on every row (printed p. 87).
the basin cost die size: d6, d6, d6, d4, d4, d4, d4, d6, d10 (printed p. 87).
the pedestal cost in gp: 200 through 2,000, a flat fee (printed p. 87).
